sentences.text:
This criminal revision under Section 397 read with Section 401 of Cr.P.C., 1973 is preferred being aggrieved by the order dated 03.05.2017 passed in CRA No.504/2014 by 14th Additional Sessions Judge, Indore arising out of the judgment dated 21.06.2014 passed in RCT No.690/2004 by Special Magistrate, Municipal Corporation, Indore whereby the revision petitioner/ accused has been convicted under Section 16(1)(a)(1) read with Section 7(1)(5) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and has been sentenced for 06 months R.I. with fine of Rs.1000/- with default stipulation of two months R.I.
2.

The proceedings disclosed that at the time of judgment by the appellate Court on 03.05.2017, this revision petitioner was not present and the judgment was passed in his absence and an application under Section 317 of the Cr.P.C., 1973 was preferred by the revision petitioner.

This revision petition was preferred on 16.05.2017, but thereafter no one appeared for the petitioner for a long period and vide order dated 06.10.2018, Amicus Currie was appointed to address the Court on behalf of the revision petitioner.

4. As per the order sheet dated 01.08.2024, a report was called from the Superintendent of Jail,
Indore and it was intimated that the revision petitioner is not in custody in this case.

5. In the light of Deepak Sahu vs. State of M.P - 2012 (3) MPLJ 534; Pramod Kumar Dwivedi vs.
State of M.P -2021 SCC OnLine MP 5268; Mallu Prajapati vs. State of M.P - 2022 SCC OnLine MP Madansingh vs Indore Nagar Palika Nigam on 10 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47125049/
1 3533 & Daulat Singh vs. State of M.P - LAWS (SC)-2024-7-111 and the judgment dated 05.08.2025 in Satish Kumar vs. Dharmendra Sharma -Criminal Revision No.1124/25 in Satish Kumar vs.
Dharmendra Sharma-Criminal Revision No.1124/25 of the High Court of M.P Jabalpur and judgment dated 04.09.2025 in Braj Kishore vs. Gouri Shankar (deceased) through Smt.Jaijuvar in Criminal Revision No.2141/2025 reiterated that Rule 48 of Chapter 10 of the High Court of M.P Rules, 2008 is mandatory in nature.

sentences.text:
The relevant para-12 of Daulat Singh (supra) is being reproduced as under:-
12.

Significantly, the legislature having thought it fit to introduce a provision enabling a convict to seek benefit of suspension of sentence pending an appeal did so by enacting section 389 of the Code.
The Code has no provision permitting an application to seek exemption from surrender.

We are minded to hold that the omission in the Code with regard to providing an NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:6488 3 CRR-619-2017 avenue for a convict suffering a sentence to seek exemption from surrender, pending a revision, is a conscious act of the legislature.
13.

We also find that there are specific provisions in the Supreme Court Rules, 2013 providing for an application for exemption from surrendering to be made, but similar such provision is not otherwise available in the 2008 Rules framed by the High Court.
6.
Since, the the revision petitioner has not surrounded in compliance of Rule 48 of Chapter 10 of the High Court of M.P Rules, 2008.

Accordingly, in the light of Daulat Singh (supra), this criminal revision is not maintainable and the same is hereby dismissed as non-maintainable.
7.
The learned trial Court is directed to ensure surrender of the revision petitioner by means of any coercive action for undergoing the jail sentence.
8. A copy of this order be sent to the learned trial Court as well as appellate Court for information.

(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE amit Madansingh vs Indore Nagar Palika Nigam on 10 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47125049/
